### 2.14 `claude/CER_Sweep_Suite_Source.md`

#### C.E.R. — Sweep Suite (Source Text, Verbatim)

**Provenance:** Authored by ChatGPT, pasted into the Claude session by Wesley on 2026-09-18, with an explicit instruction to confirm and integrate every sweep proposed here into C.E.R.'s official sweep methodology. Preserved verbatim per standing archival philosophy (nothing silently discarded or rewritten out of the historical record). The organized, cross-referenced synthesis built from this text lives in `CER_Sweep_Suite_FullTaxonomy.md` — read that one for day-to-day use; this doc is the source of record.

---

Absolutely. We have **more than just a "mod optimization sweep."** Over the course of building C.E.R., we've effectively developed a multi-pass pack-development methodology.

I'd organize the full process like this.

#### C.E.R. Pack Optimization / Development Sweep Suite

##### 1. **MMI Sweep — Master Mod Index Sweep**

The foundational pass. We take every mod source we have (current MMI, previous mod lists, candidate mods, mods from packs we've played, individual recommendations, confirmed additions, "maybe" mods, dependency mods, compatibility mods) and reconcile them into **one canonical Master Mod Index**.

Checks: duplicate mods, duplicate versions, renamed mods, Fabric/Forge/NeoForge variants, client/server-only status, dependencies, libraries, compatibility addons, Cobblemon addons, obsolete entries, questionable entries, mods that exist only because another mod was present in an old pack.

This is the sweep Claude should **never treat as just a mod list cleanup.** It is essentially our master inventory.

##### 2. **Mod List Deduplication Sweep**

Separate from the MMI itself. Asks: "Are we actually counting the same thing more than once?" Resolves duplicate names, aliases, forks, renamed projects, version variants, bundled functionality, compatibility addons mistaken for independent features.

##### 3. **Dependency / Library Sweep**

For every candidate mod: what does it require, and do we actually need those requirements? Identifies required/optional dependencies, libraries, APIs, compatibility layers, bundled libraries, duplicate libraries, unnecessary dependency chains — the **true footprint**, not merely the advertised mod.

##### 4. **Redundancy Sweep**

For every mod/system: "Is something else already doing this?" — comparing functionality, not names. Applies to storage, worldgen, structures, maps, quests, UI, inventory, mobs, Pokémon mechanics, magic, automation, performance, exploration, building, transportation, progression.

##### 5. **Functionality Overlap Sweep**

Related to redundancy but more granular — maps partial overlap between mods that aren't strict duplicates but collectively create excessive overlap. Especially useful for magic systems, worldgen, Pokémon utility, combat, storage, progression, structures.

##### 6. **Feature Saturation Sweep**

Asks: even if every mod is individually good, are we putting too much of this particular thing into the pack? Evaluates density of functionality (e.g. biome/cave/structure/terrain/dimension mods collectively), not just duplication.

##### 7. **Implementation Layer Sweep**

For every desired feature: what is the lowest-complexity layer capable of implementing it correctly? (Vanilla → Datapack → KubeJS → existing mod config → existing mod integration → custom addon → custom mod.) Don't automatically choose the most powerful solution. This is the principle already touched on for Affinity, applied across the entire pack.

##### 8. **KubeJS vs Mod vs Datapack Sweep**

A specialized version of #7. For every custom mechanic: can vanilla do it? If no, can a datapack? If no, can KubeJS? If no, can an existing mod/addon? If no, do we actually need it badly enough for custom development? Prevents C.E.R. from becoming "a giant pile of scripts recreating half of Minecraft."

##### 9. **Configuration-First Sweep**

Before scripting something, check whether the existing mod can already be configured to do it. Configuration is almost always preferable to behavioral patching.

##### 10. **Compatibility Sweep**

For every retained mod: Minecraft/NeoForge/Cobblemon version, required APIs, known incompatibilities, client/server compatibility, worldgen/rendering/entity/recipe/datapack conflicts, scripting compatibility, dependency conflicts. Does it actually work with our exact environment, not just "does it exist."

##### 11. **Cobblemon Compatibility Sweep**

Its own pass because Cobblemon is the primary game layer. Checks every relevant mod against Cobblemon 1.7.3's entities, battles, capture, spawning, drops, moves, abilities, evolution, breeding, riding, storage, interaction, rendering, animations, worldgen. Generic Minecraft-compatible mods can still be a bad fit for Cobblemon.

##### 12. **Cobblemon Ecosystem Sweep**

Separate from compatibility — maps what functionality already exists across the entire Cobblemon ecosystem (progression, exploration, catching, breeding, storage, battling, interaction, cosmetics, marks, loot, quests, research, worldgen, structures, utility, UI, immersion) so addons aren't treated as isolated discoveries.

##### 13. **Worldgen Conflict Sweep**

Checks whether overworld terrain, biomes, caves, cliffs, structures, villages, dungeons, ores, dimensions, sky generation, Aero Islands, Pokémon structures, and modded structures coexist, compete, overwrite, or multiply into nonsense — especially important given Aero Islands' high-altitude generation layered above the Overworld.

##### 14. **Worldgen Density / Chaos Sweep**

Different from compatibility: even if everything works, is the resulting world too busy? Checks structure/dungeon/village frequency, biome diversity, terrain extremes, cave density, sky structures, points of interest, exploration pacing. Goal: the world feels intentionally authored, not just non-crashing.

##### 15. **Progression Redundancy Sweep**

Maps every progression mechanism (Pokémon, quest, technology, magic, exploration, research, boss, Affinity, Fracture, Legendary) and asks whether they reinforce or compete for the player's attention — important given C.E.R.'s several meta-progression systems.

##### 16. **Progression Gate Sweep**

For every major gate: what unlocks it, is that requirement reasonable, and is another system accidentally bypassing it?

##### 17. **Progression Bypass Sweep**

Looks for alternative crafting recipes, loot, trades, structures, drops, duplication mechanics, machine/magic shortcuts, quest rewards, alternate dimensions that let a player obtain something substantially earlier than intended.

##### 18. **Recipe / Acquisition Sweep**

For every important item, builds a full acquisition map (crafting, loot, quest, drops, structure, trade, machine, magic, exploration, reward) and flags accidental duplicates, infinite sources, unintended early access, impossible acquisition, recipe conflicts, useless recipes.

##### 19. **Economy Sweep**

Checks the pack's resource economy — ores, ingots, gems, rare materials, drops, currency, loot, automation, machine outputs, quest rewards — for what's scarce, abundant, becomes infinite, or becomes trivial through automation.

##### 20. **Automation / Infinite Resource Sweep**

The more aggressive economy check: for important resources, can it be farmed/duplicated/generated/automated/converted/transmuted/obtained elsewhere — and is the resulting infinite loop intended, acceptable, progression-breaking, or completely broken?

##### 21. **Loot Table Sweep**

Checks vanilla, mod, Cobblemon, structure, drop, and reward loot for duplicates, overpowered/useless rewards, progression skips, unintended resources, conflicting tables.

##### 22. **Quest Sweep**

Inspects quest structure (intro → early game → exploration → Cobblemon → technology → magic → Affinity → Fracture → endgame) for redundant quests, missing quests, unclear objectives, rewards, gates, XP, item/command rewards, hidden mechanics, discovery pacing.

##### 23. **Quest Reward Economy Sweep**

Separate from quest structure: are FTB rewards accidentally becoming the optimal way to acquire everything, undermining the rest of the pack's economy?

##### 24. **Mod Purpose Sweep**

Every mod should answer "why is this here?" (core infrastructure, Cobblemon enhancement, progression, exploration, immersion, building, QoL, performance, C.E.R. mechanic, technical dependency). If we can't articulate the purpose, it goes into review.

##### 25. **"Cool But Doesn't Belong" Sweep**

A mod can be excellent, popular, polished, and fun and still not belong in this pack. The question: does this reinforce C.E.R.'s identity? Prevents feature creep.

##### 26. **"Can We Actually Use This?" Sweep**

For a mod whose concept is perfect but implementation questionable: can we configure/script/integrate it, does its API expose what we need, does its version support us, can it coexist with our other systems?

##### 27. **M.M.I. Confidence Sweep**

Every MMI entry gets a confidence state — CONFIRMED / LIKELY / POTENTIAL / UNVERIFIED / REJECTED — so "Claude mentioned this once" is never mistaken for "confirmed for the pack."

##### 28. **Candidate → Confirmed Promotion Sweep**

The path a candidate takes to become CONFIRMED: Research → Compatibility verified → Functionality verified → Integration verified → Pack fit verified → CONFIRMED.

##### 29. **Feature-to-Mod Coverage Sweep**

Starts from the design rather than the mod list: for every desired C.E.R. feature, which mod provides it? If none, can KubeJS? If no, datapacks? If no, is custom development required? The reverse of the MMI sweep.

##### 30. **Integration Opportunity Sweep**

Instead of "should we add another mod," asks "can two existing mods be connected to produce something neither provides alone?" Extremely C.E.R., since the project is trying to build systems *between* mods.

##### 31. **Replacement-vs-Integration Sweep**

For a new mod: does it replace an existing system, or complement it? If replacing, compare total footprint. If complementing, confirm both are justified.

##### 32. **Client QoL Saturation Sweep**

Looks across UI, tooltip, inventory, keybind, map, HUD, navigation, accessibility, and cosmetic mods for duplicate functionality, UI clutter, unnecessary overlays, keybind conflicts, excessive information density.

##### 33. **Keybind / Input Sweep**

Especially important given Smart Key Prompts / Keybind Hider / Keybind Atlas exploration — checks duplicate keys, unbound functionality, conflicting keys, category clutter, controller conflicts, QTE inputs, hidden/contextual keybinds, so controls don't become a 300-entry disaster.

##### 34. **Performance Sweep**

Multi-level: mod-level (heavy worldgen, entity/particle/rendering/AI-heavy mods, tick-heavy automation, polling scripts), system-level (interactions between them), script-level (event frequency, tick handlers, entity/world scans, scoreboard/NBT ops).

##### 35. **Tick / Polling Sweep**

Specialized performance audit: does a recurring script really need to run every tick? Prefer event / scheduled interval / state change over polling. Particularly relevant to Affinity — don't poll thresholds every tick; update state, compare old/new, trigger on crossing.

##### 36. **Server Tick Cost Sweep**

Separate from general performance: entity counts, AI, chunk ticking, block entities, machines, automation, scripts, Pokémon, worldgen, structures — a pack can have fine FPS while murdering server TPS.

##### 37. **Chunk Loading Sweep**

Checks chunk loaders, machines, farms, Pokémon systems, dimensions, Aero Islands, structures, persistent entities for unintended permanently-loaded areas.

##### 38. **Entity Population Sweep**

Especially important for Cobblemon — Pokémon spawn rates, hostile/passive mobs, modded creatures, structure entities, NPCs, decorative entities — whether the combined ecosystem creates pathological entity counts.

##### 39. **Memory / RAM Sweep**

Redundant libraries, giant worldgen systems, huge resource packs, entity-heavy mods, excessive caches, client rendering overhead, excessive dimensions, large structures — separate concern from TPS.

##### 40. **Startup / Load-Time Sweep**

What makes the pack take forever to start: datapack loading, KubeJS startup scripts, recipe/worldgen registration, resource loading, model/texture count, large registries.

##### 41. **Crash / Error Sweep**

Every crash categorized (mod bug, dependency issue, config issue, script error, worldgen conflict, entity issue, rendering issue, memory issue, version mismatch) and checked for whether it indicates a deeper architectural problem, not just "remove the crashing mod."

##### 42. **Log Spam Sweep**

Periodic cleanup of WARN/ERROR/repeated-exception/failed-lookup/missing-registry spam from mods that don't crash but destroy the server log.

##### 43. **Version Drift Sweep**

Periodically checks Minecraft/NeoForge/Cobblemon/KubeJS/Cobblemon KubeJS Bridge/FTB/major gameplay mod versions against all addon versions — catches "worked three months ago, one dependency changed since."

##### 44. **Update Regression Sweep**

After major updates: before → update → compatibility audit → gameplay audit → quest audit → script audit → worldgen audit. A successful launch doesn't mean the pack still works correctly.

##### 45. **Config Conflict Sweep**

Two mods independently configuring something that interacts badly — spawn settings, loot, worldgen, mob caps, rendering, difficulty, recipes, inventories, keybinds, dimensions.

##### 46. **Datapack Priority / Load Order Sweep**

Once C.E.R. has substantial custom datapack content: namespace collisions, tags, function ordering, recipe/loot/advancement overrides, load order, pack priority.

##### 47. **Script Namespace / Architecture Sweep**

For KubeJS specifically — organize systems into a real folder structure (e.g. `CER/affinity/`, `CER/fracture/`, `CER/resonance/`, `CER/titan/`, `CER/quests/`, `CER/world/`, `CER/cobblemon/`, `CER/integration/`) rather than ad hoc script files, and periodically audit for duplicated functions, dead code, abandoned experiments, conflicting listeners, global variables, unnecessary polling, hardcoded values.

##### 48. **Hardcoded Value Sweep**

Finds values (thresholds, percentages, durations) hardcoded across multiple scripts and moves shared design constants into centralized configuration, so changing one number doesn't require hunting down every copy.

##### 49. **State Ownership Sweep**

The Affinity lesson generalized: for every piece of information, who owns this state (Affinity → C.E.R., quest completion → FTB, species data → Cobblemon, world state → C.E.R./Minecraft)? Avoid two systems independently believing they own the same value.

##### 50. **Single Source of Truth Sweep**

Stricter version: is the same information stored in multiple places (e.g. Affinity in KubeJS NBT + scoreboard + FTB quest progress + item NBT)? One is authoritative; everything else is derived/display/integration state.

##### 51. **State Synchronization Sweep**

For any intentionally-mirrored data (Persistent Data → Scoreboard → HUD): when does sync occur, what happens after restart/death/dimension change/external data change/late join?

##### 52. **Save / Restart Persistence Sweep**

For every custom C.E.R. system: does it survive logout, server restart, world reload, dimension travel, death, chunk unload, backup restoration? Critical for Affinity.

##### 53. **Multiplayer / Server Scope Sweep**

Is a mechanic player-specific, team-specific, region-specific, dimension-specific, world-wide, or server-wide? Prevents Player A's action changing Player B's progression, or a "should be global" restoration effect accidentally scoping to one player.

##### 54. **FTB Teams Interaction Sweep**

Because C.E.R. uses Teams: individual vs. team progression, shared quest completion, shared rewards, team-owned vs. player-owned systems — especially before tying Affinity into quests.

##### 55. **Exploit Sweep**

Intentionally try to break every major system: for Affinity — can I repeatedly release/catch, automate it, reset it, multiply rewards, have multiple players trigger it? For progression — can I get a reward twice, move/duplicate items between players? One of the most important late-stage sweeps.

##### 56. **AFK / Automation Abuse Sweep**

What happens if the player leaves the game running for 12 hours — Affinity farming, mob/Pokémon farming, chunk loaders, machines, passive rewards, decay exploits, event generation.

##### 57. **Player Behavior Sweep**

Not a technical exploit test — if I were a normal player, what behavior would the mechanics naturally encourage? If the optimal behavior is absurd (stand at one machine for three hours), the design may need revision.

##### 58. **Discovery / Prescription Sweep**

Uniquely important to C.E.R.'s Discovery Over Prescription philosophy: does the pack let players discover mechanics, or does the quest book just tell them everything? Audits quest spoilers, hidden mechanics, unexplained systems, environmental/NPC clues, structures, item descriptions, visual feedback, progression revelations.

##### 59. **Lore / Mechanics Consistency Sweep**

Every major mechanic should make sense in the C.E.R. fiction — why does Affinity exist, why Fracture, why a Resonance Anchor, why can Fractured Pokémon do unusual things? Gameplay shouldn't feel like unrelated mods stapled together.

##### 60. **Thematic Cohesion Sweep**

The ultimate question: does this still feel like C.E.R.? Not "is this mod fun" or "is this popular," but does it contribute to the world being built.

##### 61. **"Remove One Mod" Sweep**

For every questionable mod: if we remove this, what actually breaks? "Nothing meaningful" is valuable information — sometimes the best optimization is deletion, not replacement.

##### 62. **"What Are We Missing?" Sweep**

The opposite exercise: starting from the intended experience, what important capability currently has no provider? Catches gaps a conventional mod audit misses.

##### 63. **Integration Gap Sweep**

After mapping all existing systems: which two systems *should* interact but currently don't (Magic↔Pokémon, Affinity↔Worldgen, Affinity↔Quests, Fracture↔Synchro, Titan↔QTE, Aero Islands↔Affinity)?

##### 64. **Custom Mechanics Feasibility Sweep**

Before committing to an ambitious feature: can existing mod/config/datapack/KubeJS/integration/addon do it, or would custom development be justified? Classify: Easy / Moderate / Complex / Stretch / Future / Reject.

##### 65. **Proof-of-Concept Sweep**

Before fully implementing a complex system, build the smallest possible prototype (for Affinity: 1 type → 1 player value → 1 world value → 1 event → 1 threshold → 1 scoreboard mirror). If it works, expand. Same philosophy for Fracture, Titan encounters, QTEs, spell integration, Aero Islands interactions.

##### 66. **Vertical Slice Sweep**

Once a system passes the prototype stage: build one complete end-to-end example (catch → Affinity calc → World+Player update → threshold → visual feedback → quest recognition → reward) rather than implementing all 18 Affinities before knowing whether one actually works.

##### 67. **End-to-End Integration Sweep**

After individual systems work: does the entire chain work (Cobblemon → KubeJS → C.E.R. → Affinity → FTB → Quest → Reward → next progression stage)? Catches integration bugs individual mod testing won't.

##### 68. **Player Experience Sweep**

Play the pack as a player, not the developer: what do I know/not know, what feels rewarding/tedious/confusing/pointless/too fast/too slow/magical/like modpack bureaucracy?

##### 69. **Fresh-World Sweep**

Start from a completely clean world, no dev commands, no prior knowledge, follow the intended experience — catches missing onboarding, accidental dependencies, broken early progression, hidden requirements, bad quest ordering, worldgen problems, confusing systems.

##### 70. **New Player / Blind Playtest Sweep**

Even better than Fresh-World: have someone who doesn't know the architecture try it, without explaining the systems, to see whether they discover them — the strongest test of Discovery Over Prescription.

##### 71. **Endgame / Long-Term Loop Sweep**

The opposite-of-fresh perspective: after 20/50/100+ hours, what remains meaningful, what becomes trivial/obsolete/repetitive, does Affinity/Pokémon/exploration/automation still matter, is there a reason to continue?

##### 72. **Modpack Identity Sweep**

At milestones: if we removed the mod names and showed someone only the gameplay systems, what would C.E.R. actually be? Prevents drifting into "generic kitchen-sink pack + Cobblemon."

##### 73. **Final Pre-Release Sweep**

The final monster — runs MMI → Dependencies → Compatibility → Redundancy → Worldgen → Progression → Recipes → Loot → Economy → Performance → Scripts → Quests → Exploits → Multiplayer → Persistence → Fresh world → Player experience, in order, then freezes the build.

---

#### The important distinction: these are NOT all the same kind of sweep

Organized into **seven major families**:

**A. Inventory / Mod Audits** — 1 MMI Sweep, 2 Deduplication Sweep, 3 Dependency Sweep, 43 Version Drift Sweep, 24 Mod Purpose Sweep, 27 MMI Confidence Sweep

**B. Functionality Audits** — 4 Redundancy Sweep, 5 Functionality Overlap Sweep, 6 Feature Saturation Sweep, 24 Mod Purpose Sweep, 29 Feature-to-Mod Coverage Sweep, 31 Replacement-vs-Integration Sweep

**C. Architecture Audits** — 7 Implementation Layer Sweep, 8 KubeJS/Datapack/Mod Sweep, 9 Configuration-First Sweep, 49 State Ownership Sweep, 50 Single Source of Truth Sweep, 51 State Synchronization Sweep, 47 Script Architecture Sweep, 48 Hardcoded Value Sweep

**D. Gameplay / Progression Audits** — 15 Progression Sweep, 16 Progression Gate Sweep, 17 Progression Bypass Sweep, 18 Recipe/Acquisition Sweep, 21 Loot Sweep, 22 Quest Sweep, 23 Quest Economy Sweep, 19 Economy Sweep, 20 Automation/Infinite Resource Sweep, 57 Player Behavior Sweep

**E. Technical / Performance Audits** — 10 Compatibility Sweep, 11 Cobblemon Compatibility Sweep, 13 Worldgen Conflict Sweep, 14 Worldgen Density Sweep, 34 Performance Sweep, 35 Tick/Polling Sweep, 36 Server TPS Sweep, 37 Chunk Loading Sweep, 38 Entity Population Sweep, 39 Memory Sweep, 40 Startup Sweep, 41 Crash/Error Sweep, 42 Log Spam Sweep, 44 Config Conflict Sweep... wait 45, 46 Datapack Priority Sweep

**F. Exploitation / Reliability Audits** — 55 Exploit Sweep, 56 AFK/Automation Abuse Sweep, 53 Multiplayer Scope Sweep, 54 FTB Teams Interaction Sweep, 52 Save/Restart Persistence Sweep, 44 Update Regression Sweep

**G. C.E.R. Design / Experience Audits** — 30 Integration Opportunity Sweep, 63 Integration Gap Sweep, 64 Custom Mechanics Feasibility Sweep, 65 Proof-of-Concept Sweep, 66 Vertical Slice Sweep, 67 End-to-End Integration Sweep, 58 Discovery vs Prescription Sweep, 59 Lore/Mechanics Consistency Sweep, 60 Thematic Cohesion Sweep, 61 "Cool But Doesn't Belong" Sweep, 26 "Can We Actually Use This?" Sweep, 61 "Remove One Mod" Sweep, 62 "What Are We Missing?" Sweep, 68 Player Experience Sweep, 69 Fresh World Sweep, 70 Blind Playtest Sweep, 71 Endgame Sweep, 72 Modpack Identity Sweep, 73 Final Pre-Release Sweep

---

#### A few **meta-processes** to explicitly add to the methodology

**The Reverse Audit** — instead of "what does this mod give us," ask "what does our design require, and where does each requirement come from?"

**The Interaction Audit** — not "does Mod A work" but "does Mod A + Mod B + C.E.R. work?" Conventional compatibility testing isn't sufficient once systems are this cross-dependent.

**The Ownership Audit** — for every important variable, who owns this? (The lesson Affinity's design surfaced, generalized to everything.)

**The Integration Value Audit** — a mod shouldn't only be judged by standalone feature count; ask how many useful C.E.R. interactions it unlocks. A small mod plugging into five systems can beat a giant standalone content mod.

**The Complexity Budget Audit** — every new system costs development complexity, configuration complexity, player learning, UI complexity, performance, troubleshooting, compatibility surface, and maintenance. Adding something spends from a finite complexity budget — a different question from "is this feature cool?"

**The Maintenance Debt Sweep** — at milestones: what have we created that future-us is going to hate maintaining (scattered constants, manually-duplicated data, overlapping mods, fragile scripts, undocumented commands, unnecessary patches, exact-version-dependent systems)? Keeps C.E.R. from becoming unmaintainable.

---

#### The actual C.E.R. development loop

```
DESIGN
↓
WHAT DO WE WANT?
↓
REVERSE AUDIT
↓
WHAT PROVIDES IT?
↓
MMI / MOD AUDIT
↓
REDUNDANCY / OVERLAP
↓
COMPATIBILITY AUDIT
↓
IMPLEMENTATION AUDIT
↓
CONFIG / DATAPACK / KUBEJS / MOD
↓
POC / PROTOTYPE
↓
VERTICAL SLICE
↓
INTEGRATION TEST
↓
PROGRESSION / ECONOMY
↓
EXPLOIT / ABUSE
↓
PERFORMANCE / TPS
↓
MULTIPLAYER / SAVE
↓
PLAYER EXPERIENCE
↓
FRESH WORLD TEST
↓
IDENTITY / COHESION
↓
SHIP
```

And after major additions, don't rerun every possible audit from scratch — run a **targeted regression sweep** against everything the new feature could have touched. Example: adding Affinity triggers Architecture, State Ownership, Cobblemon integration, FTB integration, Quest progression, Economy, Exploit, Performance, Persistence, Multiplayer, Discovery, and UI checks — not a blind retest of every building mod in the pack.

This gives a repeatable C.E.R. engineering process for deciding what enters the pack, how it's implemented, how it integrates, and whether it stays healthy as the pack grows.

Datapack uses identified: resource economy (Resin/Affinity Metal recipes), custom progression via advancements, research unlock logic (not the UI itself), Pokémon research tasks, biome affinity distribution, custom loot, recipes, advancements, structures (with caution), NOT worldgen overhauls (prefer established mods). Core" datapack (data/cobblemon_er/ with advancement, recipe, loot_table, function, predicate, tags, worldgen), split into modules only if needed (Progression/Economy/Research/Recipes/World). Yatters Biospheres reframed at Wesley's request from "dream world" into **Lost/Corrupted Biomes**: ecosystems corrupted long ago and severed from reality into isolated biospheres (quarantine, not creation). Corruption spectrum: Healthy→Tainted→Corrupted→Lost. Restoration choice mechanic proposed: Purify (restore to Overworld) / Stabilize (keep isolated, preserved) / Harness (control corruption deliberately — produces corrupted Pokémon, unusual forms, unique resources, altered evolution, dangerous encounters — ties into Affinity/research). Corruption made bidirectional: Biosphere→Overworld (restoration) AND Overworld→Biosphere (a healthy biome can destabilize, get corrupted, and become quarantined during play — dynamic world-history mechanic). Titans reframed as possible ecosystem anchors: some Titans are why a Lost ecosystem still exists at all; defeating/capturing one destabilizes it and unlocks restoration research. Lore hierarchy: Normal Biomes → Corrupted Biomes → Lost Biomes → Biospheres/Quarantine Zones → Research & Restoration → Reintroduction to Overworld, with "what caused the corruption" flagged as a late-game mystery, not to be explained early.

Aero Islands reframed at Wesley's request from "replace Overworld" into a **vertical ecological layer above the existing Overworld+worldgen mods**: ground level = normal Overworld/Cobblemon ecology; cloud layer = transition; Aero Islands = high-altitude Flying/Dragon/Electric/Psychic/Ice ecosystem with its own low/mid/high/extreme-altitude danger and rarity gradient, ruins, and potential Titan encounters; technical caveat that Aero Islands currently replaces world generation outright rather than layering, so genuine layering requires integration work (biome tags/datapacks, Lithostitched dependency) rather than a drop-in install. World architecture settled as three coexisting layers: Aero Islands (the world above), Yatters/Lost Biomes (the worlds that were lost), primary worldgen (the world people live in) — design principle: "don't let worldgen mods replace each other; give each one a physical place, ecological purpose, or narrative reason to exist."

COBBLEMON: ECOLOGICAL RESONANCE
FULL SWEEP / TRISWEEP — CHANGE LOG

SWEEP STATUS: Completed as a reconstruction pass; implementation phase NOT entered.
Scope: Four supplied archive sources: pt1, pt2, pt3, and the JavaScript/KubeJS example archive. This pass compares the recovered corpus against the current reconstructed project baseline and records deltas, new proposals, contradictions, terminology movement, and implementation candidates.
1. Executive Result — What the Full Sweep Changed
The full sweep does not overturn the project's central architecture. Instead, it exposes several layers that the compact reconstruction underrepresented. The biggest difference is that E.R. is not merely a collection of mechanics; the archive repeatedly describes a design methodology for how mechanics should teach, interact, and earn their complexity.
The core architecture remains intact: Ecological Resonance, 18 Affinities, World vs Trainer Affinity, Resonance, Restoration Engine, dynamic spawning, research, Pokémon variants, materials, factions/activities, and Legendary Domains.
The design philosophy is stronger than previously captured: Creation Over Crafting, Discovery Over Prescription, consequence-based teaching, Special Does Not Mean 'Bigger Number', and Player Leaves a Mark.
A new explicit design rule is recoverable: Justified Complexity Rule — complexity is acceptable only when it has a clear ecological, biological, physical, technological, Resonance, narrative, or gameplay justification.
Affinity Relationships emerge as a useful banked concept: meaningful world-level interactions among Affinities, explicitly not derived mechanically from the Pokémon battle type chart.
The variant architecture is substantially clearer: Identity → Form → Phenotype → State → Anomaly, with compatibility rules rather than a flat mutually-exclusive list.
Research is more developed than the compact reconstruction showed. The Field Journal, Memory Phenomena, Type Memories, fossils, photographs, retirement records, and observation-driven leads form one knowledge system.
Resonance Processing is a major recovered technical/gameplay concept: Pokémon can actively perform work on machines through moves, with machine Drives supplying functional specialization.
The full sweep also recovered a mature archive-governance layer: Modification Sweep, Integration Sweep, Mod Audit, TriSweep, Full Sweep, Bank Sweep, Missing Link Integration, Dependency Sweep, provenance rules, and change logging.
Several implementation-era ideas are now explicitly marked as candidates rather than canon: dynamic starter/New Game Plus logic, automatically shifting active affinity slots, dynamic individual quest injection, custom Resonance Marks, earned ranks, and universal Apricorn Ingots with provenance.
2. Status / Evidence Rules Used in This Sweep
The source corpus contains both historical discussion and later reconstruction language. A later paragraph was not automatically treated as canonical merely because it appears later in a document. Evidence, explicit acceptance/rejection, and current project context were weighed separately.
Status
Meaning in this sweep

PROVISIONAL / CURRENT PROPOSAL
Current direction that still needs final design confirmation.
HISTORICAL
Genuine earlier idea preserved for chronology and reuse.
SUPERSEDED
Replaced by a later terminology or architecture.
REJECTED / OBSOLETE
Explicitly discarded or made unnecessary by later architecture.
DORMANT
Not active, but potentially reusable.
UNRESOLVED / CONTRADICTORY
The archive contains competing interpretations or the current status cannot be safely inferred.
ARCHIVAL UNKNOWN
Mentioned, but insufficient source evidence exists to classify it further.

3. Modification Sweep — Changes to the Reconstructed Architecture
3.1 Core philosophy — strengthened, not replaced
The full sweep confirms that the eight major pillars are mutually reinforcing rather than independent slogans.
Creation Over Crafting (C.O.C.)
The World Is Alive
Restoration Is Progression
Resonance Connects Everything
Discovery Over Prescription
Pokémon Are More Than Battle Units
Special Does Not Mean 'Bigger Number'
The Player Leaves a Mark
NEWLY FORMALIZED SUPPORTING PRINCIPLE — Systems should teach the player about the world by demonstrating their consequences.
This is strongly reflected in the archive's treatment of Eevee, Castform, scanners, research, Twisted Pokémon, ecological change, and hidden discoveries. It should be treated as a design-evaluation rule, not merely flavor.
3.2 Justified Complexity Rule — recovered as a formal design filter
The archive explicitly defines a rule under which a mechanic, relationship, variant, exception, layer, or system may be proposed when it has a clear ecological, biological, physical, technological, Resonance, narrative, or gameplay justification and integrates coherently with the existing design.
Sweep classification: STRONG RECONSTRUCTION / DESIGN RULE.
Important consequence: The project should not reject complexity simply because it is complex; it should reject complexity that has no job.
3.3 Affinity Relationships — new formal candidate
The archive contains a specific request to preserve the term 'Affinity Relationship' for later use and a later sweep definition for it. It describes a meaningful relationship between two or more World Affinities that can create ecological, environmental, biological, technological, or Resonance interactions.

Constraint preserved: not every pair must interact, and a relationship should have a world-level reason. The archive explicitly rejects using the battle type chart as the justification.
3.4 Pokémon taxonomy — major architectural clarification
The full sweep recovers a much cleaner layered taxonomy than a flat list of Normal / Alpha / Shadow / Fractured / Fusion / Fake.

The archive then proposes a compatibility matrix so combinations are possible where meaningful without turning the system into an exhaustive checklist. Examples recovered include Shadow Fusion, Alpha + Shadow as rare, Fusion + Fracture, and other controlled combinations.
Sweep classification: STRONG ARCHITECTURAL PROPOSAL; exact implementation taxonomy remains unresolved.
Important distinction: Alpha, Shadow, Fractured, Fusion, and Fake should each answer a different gameplay question rather than merely increase power.
3.5 Research — upgraded from a subsystem to a project-wide knowledge layer
The full sweep shows Research repeatedly functioning as the connective tissue between observation and discovery.
Field Journal records encounters, captures, releases, reintroductions, variants, Twisted forms, behavior, habitats, photography, Affinity, migration, Resonance Phenomena, materials, fossils, anomalies, history, and eventually Domains.
Research should unlock leads and methods rather than merely award Research XP.
A photograph or observation can create a lead, which can lead to a material, spawning condition, Affinity interaction, recipe, restoration technique, historical event, behavior discovery, or Legendary information.
Type Memories are knowledge artifacts: Type Gem = condensed Affinity; Type Plate = control; Liquid Affinity = manipulation/transport; Terra Shard = anchoring; Type Memory = understanding.
Resonance Fossils can preserve multiple 'memory channels' and connect Fossil → Memory → Research → Affinity understanding.
Retirement Records can preserve the documented history of a Pokémon after retirement, allowing an optional donation/research path without reducing the Pokémon's life to an XP reward.
Sweep classification: STRONG RECONSTRUCTION / CURRENT DESIGN DIRECTION.
3.6 Resonance Processing — newly elevated integration
The source corpus contains a developed concept that was not adequately represented in the compact baseline: Resonance Processing is the refinement of materials, items, fluids, and related inputs through Resonance Machines.
Component

Pokémon

Machine capability / modular function

Upgrade/interface allowing specialized Drives

A representative archive example: place an Apricorn in a furnace-like machine with an ingot cast, then have a Fire Pokémon use a Fire move to provide thermal processing instead of using ordinary fuel. The archive explicitly treats this as a strong C.O.C. example.
Accepted source pieces recovered: Resonance Processing / Resonance Machines; move quality can affect processing yield.
Status: STRONG CURRENT PROPOSAL; exact machine implementation and Drive list remain open.
3.7 Apricorn Ingot — new material-design proposal
The archive develops a particularly interesting material-bloat solution. Instead of creating seven near-identical permanent ingot items, all Apricorn colors can produce a common 'Apricorn Ingot' while retaining the origin of the source Apricorn.
Universal processed material: Apricorn Ingot.
Retained provenance: e.g. Origin: Red Apricorn / Origin: Black Apricorn.
Downstream functionality may inspect provenance when the ingot is processed further.
The color therefore remains meaningful without creating an inventory full of nearly identical materials.
Move quality can influence yield; weak/controlled/overpowered moves can produce different results or failure risks.
Status: CURRENT PROPOSAL / INTEGRATION CANDIDATE. Not locked as a final Apricorn implementation.
3.8 Active Trainer Affinity slots — technical proposal recovered
The JavaScript archive contains a concrete model in which all 18 personal Affinity scores are tracked, while only a limited number of active slots are functional. The script can automatically sort the player's highest Affinities and assign the top available ones to active slots.
Example progression: 1 slot initially, later 2–6 slots.
Slot 2 example requirement: at least three Affinities awakened to a threshold.
Slot 3 example requirement: cumulative World Affinity threshold.
Slot 4 example requirement: completion of a selected research-path milestone.
Slots 5–6 were proposed as late-game physical attunement items.
Organic shifting is a major feature: if Ghost eventually surpasses Water, Ghost automatically occupies the relevant higher slot.
Sweep classification: PROPOSAL / IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE, NOT LOCKED.
Reason for caution: The current design still needs a final decision on whether Trainer Affinity slots should be manually chosen, automatically ranked, or use a hybrid model.
3.9 Dynamic quest architecture — clarified
The JavaScript archive distinguishes two useful mechanisms: use FTB Quests' own visual prerequisites for ordinary linear quest progression, and use KubeJS/Game Stages for quests that depend on dynamic system variables such as Affinity, research-path choices, or world state.
Built-in FTB Quest gating: simple visual/linear dependencies.
Programmatic stage injection: system-driven hidden quests.
Individual quest visibility can be controlled rather than hiding an entire chapter.
A centralized hidden-quest evaluator can respond to Affinity thresholds and player choice flags.
Status: IMPLEMENTATION CANDIDATE; source code is illustrative and must not be treated as tested production code.
3.10 Dynamic starter / New Game Plus — recovered proposal
The JavaScript archive contains a replay-oriented starter concept: a persistent pack-completion flag survives world deletion/recreation, and a custom starter selection interface can expose additional starter options after the pack has been completed.
Base starter roster plus secret challenge/late-game starters after completion.
Persistent completion flag stored outside the individual world.
KubeJS-driven replacement/bypass of a rigid native starter screen was proposed.
This supports a New Game Plus / rogue-lite replay loop.
Status: PROPOSAL. Starter-world and starter-roster design remain unresolved.
4. Integration Sweep — Connections Strengthened by the Full Corpus
4.1 Research ↔ Retirement
Retirement is no longer only a loss-state protocol. A retired Pokémon can leave a memorial object, an optional specimen donation, and a Retirement Record preserving its life history. This directly supports the Research/Field Journal architecture.
4.2 Research ↔ Resonance Marks
Marks can function as persistent evidence of meaningful Pokémon history without being stat upgrades. The archive suggests marks such as Resonance Pioneer, First Resonance, Echo-Touched, World's Memory, and Resonant Survivor as candidates.
4.3 Memory Phenomenon ↔ Discovery Over Prescription
Memory Phenomena can reveal leads instead of directly dispensing a Pokémon. After a category such as Shadow is discovered, it can enter the possible Memory Phenomenon pool. This preserves discovery gating without inventing an extra Pokémon category.
4.4 Resonance Selection ↔ Memory Phenomenon
The distinction is now particularly clean: Resonance Selection asks 'Which Pokémon resonates with you?' while Memory Phenomenon asks 'What does the world remember?'
4.5 Z-Crystals ↔ Ecological Risk
Z-Crystals can force Affinity manifestations such as Outbreaks or temporary Overcharge. This reinforces the key lesson that forcing Resonance is not the same as restoring ecological health.
4.6 Terra Shards ↔ Z-Crystals
Terra Shards anchor/stabilize Affinity; Z-Crystals amplify/intensify it. The full sweep confirms that this functional distinction is more coherent than a conventional material tier ladder.
4.7 Pokémon ↔ Technology
Resonance Processing makes Pokémon active participants in industrial production. This is stronger than treating Pokémon as decorative companions or generic RF generators.
4.8 Materials ↔ C.O.C.
The material family remains organized by verbs: Gather, Move, Condense, Control, Anchor, Amplify, Understand, Apply, Deep Resonance. The full sweep reinforces this as a central anti-bloat rule.
4.9 Factions / Activities ↔ Player Identity
Earned ranks, paths, contests, rallies, gyms, research, ranger work, and trainer accomplishments can become evidence of what the player has actually done rather than generic XP classes.
4.10 Marks ↔ 'The World Remembers'
Resonance Marks, Memory Phenomena, abandoned structures, historical research, fossils, and Championship history all reinforce a common philosophical motif: the world contains history independent of the current inhabitants.
5. Mod Audit — Changes and Newly Recovered Mod Policy
The full sweep reveals a stronger anti-bloat and dependency discipline than the compact reconstruction previously showed.
Do not add generic quest spam.
Do not add dozens of redundant Pokémon currencies.
Avoid random loot-rarity inflation.
Avoid large quantities of unrelated structures.
Avoid machines that exist only to justify another machine.
Avoid giant weapon/armor progression unless directly justified.
Avoid generic RPG classes/stat systems that compete with the E.R. identity.
Avoid duplicate storage, map, economy, and excessive biome systems.
Prefer native NeoForge solutions when good options exist.
Fabric through a bridge is permitted only when the benefit materially outweighs compatibility cost.
Do not claim orphaned dependencies without an actual installed JAR/dependency list.

6. Archive / Governance Sweep — Newly Explicit Processes
Process
Recovered purpose
Modification Sweep
Whole-project reanalysis; may reorganize, consolidate, remove, replace, add, rebalance, rename, redefine, simplify, expand, resolve contradictions, and identify redundancy.
Integration Sweep
Analyze how systems interact, including shared resources, states, bidirectional influence, contradictions, redundancy, loops, and complexity.
Mod Audit
Review additions/removals, versions, overlap, compatibility, dependencies, missing infrastructure, and custom-work requirements.
TriSweep
Modification Sweep + Integration Sweep + Mod Audit.
Full Sweep
Umbrella term for applicable project sweeps/audits/reviews; not every sub-process must run every time.
Bank Sweep
Catalogue terminology regardless of status: official, locked, banked, candidate, working, historical, rejected, superseded, ambiguous.
Dependency Sweep
After removing a mod, recursively remove dependencies that are no longer required while preserving shared dependencies.
Missing Link Integration (M.L.I.)
Proactively identify two project elements that should interact but currently lack an integration; suggest an existing mod, new integration, or new mod concept.
Change Logging
Record meaningful reconstruction decisions, including proactive changes, vetoes, coined terms, sweeps, and integration proposals.

8. Conflicts / Reclassifications Exposed by the Full Sweep
8.1 Alpha implementation conflict
The archive's modernization pass recommends removing an external Alpha mod because Cobblemon 1.8 provides native Alpha functionality. However, the current project record also explicitly says Alpha Pokémon are included from the Pokémon Alpha mod. These are not safely reconciled by assumption.
Required final decision: At the final Mod Audit, determine whether the external Alpha mod provides unique functionality beyond native Cobblemon 1.8. If it does, document the added value; if not, the native system should likely supersede the external dependency.
Classification: CONTRADICTORY / UNRESOLVED.
8.2 Visible barren-world concept vs. degraded-world premise
The historical corpus frequently describes the world as degraded, sick, dormant, or incomplete and sometimes proposes visibly removing grass/water until restoration. The current project direction has intentionally paused the stronger 'barren until affinity' implementation.
Reconciliation: Keep 'degraded/incomplete world' as the premise while treating the specific visibly barren implementation as HISTORICAL / PAUSED. A world can be ecologically disrupted without literally deleting basic survival resources.
8.3 Resonance Core → Attunement Core terminology
The source corpus contains older Resonance Core terminology and later Attunement Core terminology. The sweep confirms these should not be silently collapsed.
Current normalization: Attunement Core is the later preferred term; Resonance Core remains historical terminology unless later evidence reopens it.
8.4 Memory Echo → Memory Phenomenon
The source corpus uses Memory Echo and Memory Phenomenon for closely related concepts. The later architecture distinguishes Memory Phenomenon as the normalized current term for world-memory discovery/event initiation.
Classification: TERMINOLOGY EVOLUTION / SUPERSEDED LABEL, not necessarily two independent systems.
8.5 Personal Affinity slot model vs. manual switching
The JavaScript archive gives a concrete automatic Top-6 model, while the broader design discussion considers active Affinity caps and a reset/switch mechanic that should remain fun. The full sweep does not choose between them.
Status: UNRESOLVED. Preserve both models until the Affinity architecture is finalized.
9. What the Full Sweep Did NOT Change
Project title remains Cobblemon: Ecological Resonance as the current preferred title.
18 fundamental Affinities remain foundational.
World Affinity and Trainer Affinity remain distinct.
Resonance remains the underlying connective phenomenon rather than a second generic mana bar.
Restoration Engine remains the custom connective architecture.
Dynamic spawning remains central.
Restoration remains progression rather than a cosmetic afterthought.
Resonance Balls and contextual capture remain central candidates.
Terra Shards remain primarily an anchoring/stabilization material.
Z-Crystals remain amplification/Overdrive candidates, including Affinity Outbreaks.
Type Plates remain control/regulation materials.
Type Memories remain research/understanding artifacts.
Resonance Drives remain modular machinery components and should not be forced into 18 variants.
Resonance Hearts remain tied to deep Resonance / Virtue / Legendary recognition rather than ordinary 18-type crafting.
Legendary progression remains recognition and Domain Authority rather than simple acquisition/stat escalation.
The Living World remains the major all-18 restoration milestone, with the 19th Observatory position intentionally mysterious.
Trainer / Researcher / Ranger remain the strongest recovered player identities; Artisan and Warden remain proposals.
The project remains in Foundation / Discovery; implementation should not begin until the final TriSweep and explicit per-system implementation announcements.

11. Updated 'Most Important Loop' After Full Sweep
World begins degraded/incomplete, not necessarily literally barren.
Player explores and observes.
Pokémon, environment, materials, and phenomena provide evidence.
Research converts evidence into understanding and leads.
Player acts: capture, release, restore, build, process, investigate, participate, or experiment.
Trainer Affinity and World Affinity respond.
Restoration Engine translates those changes into ecology, spawning, populations, phenomena, and opportunities.
The player discovers new materials and methods.
Creation / Resonance Processing turns understanding into physical infrastructure.
Pokémon become active participants in machines, ecology, research, and social activities.
Player identity emerges from what they actually do.
Virtues document demonstrated qualities rather than merely granting levels.
Legendary beings notice that accumulated history and eventually recognize the player.
Domain Authority changes what the player can understand/do.
The world remembers the player's actions through ecology, structures, marks, records, and phenomena.
12. New Open Questions Created or Clarified by the Sweep
Does native Cobblemon Alpha functionality fully replace the external Alpha mod, or does the external mod add something unique?
What exactly is the legal/meaningful compatibility matrix for layered Pokémon designations?
Should active Trainer Affinity slots be automatic, manual, or hybrid?
What are the exact Affinity Relationship rules, and which pairings genuinely deserve mechanics?
What are the final Resonance Drive functions and names?
What exactly does Resonance Processing require from Pokémon moves, and how is move quality measured?
How should Apricorn provenance influence downstream functionality without creating hidden complexity?
What is the exact relationship between Research, Type Memories, Fossils, and the Field Journal data model?
How much of Championship Protocol belongs to multiplayer/server history versus single-player memorial gameplay?
What are the final player paths, and how do paths differ from earned ranks/titles?
Does the Resonance Mark family use custom native Cobblemon marks, an independent metadata system, or both?
What is the exact implementation of Memory Phenomenon selection and how does discovery gating work?
What are the final starter worlds and starter roster?
What are the exact World Balance and World Health mechanics?
Which mod candidates survive a full current-version compatibility audit?
Which systems require custom NeoForge/KubeJS work versus existing mods?
13. Recommended Next Reconstruction Operation
The full sweep suggests that the next useful operation is not implementation. It is a final reconciliation pass over the highest-impact unresolved interfaces. The order below minimizes the chance of building one system on assumptions that another system later invalidates.
1. Freeze the reconstructed terminology layers: Official Terminology vs Term Bank vs Historical Terminology.
2. Resolve the Pokémon layered taxonomy and Alpha-mod contradiction.
3. Resolve the Affinity architecture: World, Trainer, Regional, Balance, Biodiversity, Health, and active slots.
4. Resolve Research architecture: Field Journal, Memory Phenomena, Type Memories, Fossils, photography, and Retirement Records.
5. Resolve Resonance Processing and the final material verbs/functions.
6. Resolve player identity: Paths vs Ranks vs Titles vs Virtues.
7. Resolve capture architecture and Resonance Ball/Attunement terminology.
8. Run the current mod candidate list through a version/loader/dependency audit.
9. Only after those are reconciled, perform the final implementation-entry TriSweep.
14. Source Notes
This report is a reconstruction/change-log artifact, not a replacement for the historical archive. The supplied source documents remain the historical record. The strongest newly recovered material came from pt2/pt3 and the JavaScript example archive, including the explicit TriSweep framework, Affinity Relationships, layered Pokémon taxonomy, Research/Field Journal expansion, Resonance Processing, Apricorn provenance, earned ranks, Resonance Marks, Championship Protocol, Dependency Sweep, Missing Link Integration, dynamic quest logic, active Affinity slots, and New Game Plus starter logic.
pt1 — Cobblemon Ecological Resonance Archive Reconstruction Plan (historical project/design corpus).
pt2 — Cobblemon Ecological Resonance Archive Reconstruction Plan (large reconstructed/addendum/mod/architecture corpus).
pt3 — Cobblemon Ecological Resonance Archive Reconstruction Plan (later reconstruction procedure, marks, processing, governance, compatibility, and sweep material).
Cobblemon EcoRe JavaScript example — technical examples and KubeJS implementation patterns; code is preserved as historical technical material and is not assumed tested unless independently verified.
15. Final Sweep Verdict
VERDICT: The full sweep produces more refinement than reversal. The project architecture is stronger than the compact reconstruction suggested, especially around Research, Pokémon taxonomy, Resonance Processing, archive governance, and the philosophy of justified complexity.
The most important newly visible principle is this: E.R. should not merely contain more systems. Each system should explain the world, connect to other systems, create meaningful consequences, and give the player a reason to care. The archive's strongest ideas all become more coherent when evaluated by that standard.
Implementation status remains: NOT ENTERED.

#### 5.1.5 Ecological Resonance research baseline (Cobblemon 1.8.0 era)

*File:* `783ef0fb-attachment.txt` (26,529 bytes)

Cobblemon 1.8.0 • Minecraft 1.21.1 • NeoForge • Ecological Resonance Research Baseline
Prepared as a reference document for evaluating exactly what the base Cobblemon mod already provides, what changed over time, what was removed or moved out of the core, and what can be reused as Ecological Resonance progression or reward infrastructure.
Research cutoff: September 14, 2026. The official wiki and current 1.8.0 release material were treated as the primary evidence. Where a changelog states a reason, it is labeled as explicit. Where the reason is not stated, the document does not invent one; any design interpretation is labeled as inference.
1. Executive Summary
Cobblemon 1.8.0 is substantially more than a Pokémon battle-and-capture layer. The current core already includes a persistent Pokémon simulation, a Pokédex, PC/storage, multiple battle formats, fishing, riding, cooking, Pokémon-targeted food and bait, breeding-adjacent data structures, evolution, marks, cosmetics, Pokémon AI and herds, world structures, fossil archaeology, revival machinery, Type Gems, TMs, habitats, NPCs/dialogue, configurable spawning, datapack-driven species/spawn systems, extensive commands, and a large developer-facing Molang/event API.
For Ecological Resonance, this is strategically important: many systems originally imagined as custom ER mechanics can instead be expressed as a layer on top of Cobblemon's existing hooks. The 1.8.0 baseline also makes several older plans redundant or easier to simplify. The most important native foundations for ER are spawning rules, habitats, Type Gems, Pokémon scale/Alpha state, marks, PC wallpapers, statistics/advancements, NPC party composition, dialogue, Pokémon behavior, riding, fishing, food/bait, fossil structures, and the event/Molang layer.
The historical record also shows a recurring design pattern: Cobblemon tends to add a broad foundation first, then refine it through performance work, usability changes, compatibility improvements, and data-driven APIs. That makes the archive's old ideas particularly valuable when they can be mapped onto newer native foundations instead of reimplemented from scratch.
2. Evidence & Scope
This audit is intentionally divided into four evidence levels:
CURRENT — directly documented as part of the 1.8.0 feature set or current wiki.
HISTORICAL — documented in an earlier Cobblemon release and useful for understanding how a system evolved.
REMOVED / MOVED — explicitly removed from core, deprecated, replaced, or shifted toward addon/datapack implementation.
ER OPPORTUNITY — an analytical recommendation for how Ecological Resonance could use the feature. These are not Cobblemon claims.
The phrase “every current feature” is interpreted as every meaningful player-facing, world-facing, configuration, command, datapack, and developer-facing capability that is documented by the official current wiki/release material. It does not attempt to reproduce every individual line of source code or every one of the 1,000+ Pokémon species records.
Source: Cobblemon Official Wiki — Main Page — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Main_Page
Source: Cobblemon 1.8.0 — Make Your Move Update — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.8.0
3. Current Baseline: Cobblemon 1.8.0

Source: Cobblemon 1.8.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.8.0
Source: Pokémon — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Pokemon
Source: Riding — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Pok%C3%A9mon/Riding
Source: Spawn Pool World — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Spawn_Pool_World
Source: Spawn Rules — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Spawn_Rules
4. Current Feature Catalog
4.1 Pokémon as living entities
Persistent individual Pokémon data: species, forms/aspects, level, experience, stats, IVs/EVs, nature, abilities, moves, held items, friendship, nickname, marks and other individual state.
Visual and behavioral identity: models, animations, poses, quirks, cries, sounds, particle effects, scale, gender differences, regional forms and other aspects.
Pokémon can exist in the world outside battle, interact with blocks/entities, pathfind, swim, sleep, herd, hunt, defend, intimidate, collect nectar, mount to the player, and exhibit species-specific behavior.
Pokémon can be captured, released, stored in PC boxes, sent out, recalled, traded, evolved, healed, fed, given held/cosmetic items, ridden, photographed through compatible addons, and subjected to many data-driven interactions.
Alpha Pokémon are now a distinct natural state, with size, aggression, strength, TM knowledge, herd leadership and a unique mark.
4.2 Battle
PvN/wild battles and PvP/trainer battles.
Single battles plus Double, Triple and Multi-battles.
Flat-level battle options (50, 100, 5) with no normal experience/EV reward during the flat battle mode.
Battle UI with move selection, PP, status, HP, switching, battle log, messages and requests.
Battle spectating and explicit forfeit support.
Battle-related gamerules/configuration include player invulnerability and mob-targeting behavior during battles.
Large move/ability/held-item system based on Pokémon battle data, with many visual and textual effects.
AI trainers can use party pools and party compositions, and NPCs can issue commands/animations in battle.
ER opportunity: treat battle as one of several ways to restore or test ecosystems, not the only progression axis. Native multi-battles are particularly useful for tournaments, faction battles and world events.
Source: Cobblemon 1.6.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.6.0
Source: Cobblemon 1.5.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.5
4.3 Capture & Poké Balls
Poké Ball family with multiple specialized ball behaviors.
Ball capture multipliers can depend on environmental and Pokémon conditions.
Critical captures and Pokédex registration interact with capture feedback.
Ancient Poké Balls have distinct behavior, visuals and sounds.
Ancient Feather/Wing/Jet Balls fly farther; Ancient Heavy/Leaden/Gigaton Balls are heavier and do not fly as far.
Capture feedback includes bounce/open/breakout animations and sounds.
Ball recipes are tag-based, making datapack/mod compatibility and replacement easier.
ER opportunity: this is a strong foundation for the planned Resonance Ball ecosystem. ER can add an attunement/treatment layer without replacing the base concept of specialized balls.
Source: Poké Ball history — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Heavy_Ball
Source: Ancient Poké Ball — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Ancient_Pok%C3%A9_Ball
4.4 Party, PC and storage
Party of up to six Pokémon.
PC storage with multiple boxes.
Box renaming, sorting by name/level/Pokédex number/gender/type, reverse sorting, filtering by Pokémon properties, wallpaper customization, IV/EV displays and box scrolling.
Unlockable PC wallpapers include color-based and biome-based wallpapers; custom wallpapers and custom unlock conditions can be supplied through resource/data packs.
Commands can open PC, move Pokémon, search PC, rename boxes, change wallpapers, count boxes and take Pokémon.
Pasture Blocks allow stored Pokémon to roam in a physical area.
ER opportunity: PC wallpapers are one of the best low-power rewards available because they can communicate restoration milestones without affecting combat balance.
Source: PC — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Pc
Source: Cobblemon 1.7.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.7.0
4.5 Pokédex
Craftable Pokédex that can be placed on lecterns.
Scanner interface and zoom behavior.
Species/form registration and completion statistics.
Regional/other dex groupings and grant/revoke commands.
Move Dex added in 1.8.0.
Base stats moved out of the summary and into the Pokédex.
Pokédex can be placed in Chiseled Bookshelves.
Scanning distance is configurable.
Server/datapack controls exist for hiding unimplemented species from the Pokédex.
ER opportunity: use the Pokédex as the player's first research interface, then layer Resonance observations and ecological records around it.
Source: Pokédex — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Pokedex
4.6 Progression data on Pokémon
Experience and level progression.
Friendship, including progression through interaction and effects from certain items.
IVs and EVs.
Nature.
Abilities and hidden abilities.
Moves and relearnable moves.
Evolution conditions and many different evolution requirement types.
Marks and ribbons.
Individual scale and Alpha state.
Original Trainer/provenance information.
Important limitation: the official species-data documentation still describes several move-learning methods in a data structure, while not every method is necessarily implemented as a player-facing feature. Do not assume a field existing in species JSON means the mechanic is active in survival gameplay.
Source: Species — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Species
4.7 AI, ecology and behavior
Pokémon spawn and move in herds.
Minecraft Brain-based AI supports more complex behavior.
Pastured Pokémon can sleep, approach the player and be instructed to attack hostile mobs.
Species groups can intimidate specific vanilla mobs.
Some Pokémon hunt each other and some herd together.
Some owned Pokémon defend the player.
Combee can gather nectar and deliver it to Saccharine leaves or beehives under the documented conditions.
Lightning interactions can depend on typing/abilities such as Lightning Rod, Motor Drive and Volt Absorb; Ground types are immune to lightning damage.
ER opportunity: this is a major reason not to build a completely artificial ecology simulator. Let Cobblemon supply the creature behavior and let ER change eligibility, populations, habitats and consequences.
Source: Cobblemon 1.7.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.7.0
4.8 Food, bait, medicine and Pokémon care
Campfire Pot cooking system with apricorn-colored pots.
Poké Snacks can spawn Pokémon in the wild; specific berries can influence Hidden Ability outcomes.
Poké Cakes are decorative/consumable variants and do not spawn Pokémon.
Aprijuice modifies riding characteristics according to flavor and Pokémon nature.
Local/regional foods and specialty dishes exist.
Medicines include potions, status cures, revives, roots, powders, berries and other Pokémon-care items.
Pokémon have fullness values; food given to Pokémon increases fullness, and each food has a different fullness contribution.
Many Pokémon can be interacted with using tools/items to produce resources.
ER opportunity: food is ideal for Ranger/research/restoration rewards because it can be useful without being permanently power-creeping.
Source: Cobblemon 1.7.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.7.0
Source: Pokémon — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Pokemon
4.9 Fishing
Poké Rods use a smithing-template construction and are themed by Poké Ball type.
Fishing can catch Pokémon and items.
Lure Ball improves catch rate for Pokémon caught with a fishing rod.
Repeat Ball improves catch rate for Pokémon already registered in the player's Pokédex.
Fishing-related marks can be assigned to wild-caught Pokémon.
Fishing is integrated into spawn influences and developer hooks.
ER opportunity: water restoration can unlock fishing pools, special surveys, seasonal events and aquatic research.
Source: Cobblemon 1.6.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.6.0
Source: Mark — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Mark
4.10 Riding and traversal
Rideable Pokémon do not require saddles.
Ride styles include land, liquid and air categories with multiple style implementations.
Each mount has Speed, Acceleration, Skill, Jump and Stamina riding statistics.
Different styles interpret the same riding statistics differently.
Aprijuice can alter riding characteristics.
Camera mode can be saved per ride style.
Conditional seats can be gated through Molang, including conditions such as Alpha state.
Riding statistics track land, air and liquid travel distance.
ER opportunity: unlock specialized mounts through restored habitats, Ranger progression, faction reputation or ecological milestones.
Source: Riding — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Pok%C3%A9mon/Riding
4.11 World generation and structures
Fossil dig sites and fossil-related structures.
Ruins and ancient structures.
Mini-dungeons/trial-spawner structures.
Village Pokémon Centers.
Habitat structures.
Shipwreck coves and fishing-boat discovery structures.
Evolution-stone ores and other Cobblemon world resources.
Apricorn and Saccharine wood ecosystems, berry trees, medicinal plants, crops and other natural resources.
ER opportunity: restoration can change access, loot, spawn conditions and visible state of existing structures rather than requiring every restoration location to be custom-built.
Source: Structure — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Structure
Source: Village Structures — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Village_Structures
4.12 Fossils, archaeology and resurrection
Fossils can be discovered in dedicated structures and by brushing suspicious blocks.
Data Monitor, Fossil Analyzer and Restoration Tank combine into the Resurrection Machine workflow.
Fossils can be revived into Pokémon.
Relic Coins, Gilded Chests, pottery sherds, armor trims and other archaeological rewards are part of the system.
Archaeological structures have specialized loot and visual identity.
ER opportunity: this is nearly a ready-made Researcher path. Fossil restoration can be a model for broader ER restoration procedures.
Source: Cobblemon 1.5.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.5
4.13 Type Gems and TMs
Type Gems were introduced in 1.5.0.
In 1.8.0 Type Gems entered world generation through clusters and deepslate core blocks used for growing elemental Type Gems.
TMs are crafted through the TM Machine using Type Gems.
TM recipe unlocks are tied to having Pokémon that know the move.
1.8.0 adds TM advancement triggers and a TM-learning counter.
TM use can be configured to be infinite-use, and instant unlocking of all TM recipes is configurable.
ER opportunity: Type Gems are now materially closer to the project's planned Affinity-material language than they were in the original design. Any ER material system should therefore justify why it is different from native Type Gems.
Source: Type Gems — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Type_Gems
Source: Cobblemon 1.8.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.8.0
4.14 NPCs, dialogue and trainers
NPC spawning, editing and deletion commands.
NPC party pools and party compositions.
Composed party providers.
Basic chatter behavior.
Dialogue screens and dialogue commands.
Behavior Editor for NPCs and Pokémon.
NPC trainers can use Pokémon models and Pokémon can be used in NPC-related systems.
NPC battle commands/animations and developer-facing behavior hooks.
ER opportunity: faction settlements, researchers, Rangers, gym leaders, Guardian Syndicate members, restoration workers and event organizers can all be built on native NPC infrastructure.
Source: Cobblemon 1.8.0 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.8.0
Source: Commands — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Commands
4.15 Marks, ribbons, cosmetics and visible identity
Marks from mainline Pokémon games are represented.
Wild Pokémon can receive fishing, personality, weather and time-related marks.
Partner Mark was added in 1.7.2.
Mini, Jumbo and Alpha marks were added in 1.8.0.
Pokémon markings can be toggled in the summary.
Held items can be made visibly held and cosmetic items can be assigned separately.
Certain Pokémon have special cosmetic interactions and visible item displays.
ER opportunity: marks should be treated as story/provenance/status rewards before considering raw-stat rewards.
Source: Mark — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Mark
Source: Cobblemon 1.7.2 — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/1.7.2
4.16 Data-driven modding surface
Species additions can append or replace targeted species data without replacing entire base species files.
Spawn pools, spawn detail presets and global spawn rules are datapack-driven.
Weighted choices can select randomized aspects.
Molang exposes player, Pokémon, NPC, battle, party, PC, Pokédex, spawning, server and other contexts.
Event callbacks exist for captures, evolution, healing, scanning, berry harvest, loot drops, Pokémon seen, eggs, experience, bait, Poké Rod actions, friendship, wallpaper unlocking, starter choice, EV gain, release, nickname, held items, shoulder mounting, trade, fossil revival, player ticks and more.
Species can use data components for item drops and other data-driven behavior.
NPC parties can be built from pools and compositions.
Custom wallpapers can have custom unlock conditions.
This is arguably the most important technical discovery for ER: the project can be architected as a data/event layer around Cobblemon rather than as a replacement Pokémon engine.
Source: Molang — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Molang
Source: Species Additions — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Species_Additions
Source: Spawn Rules — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Spawn_Rules
Source: Spawn Detail Presets — https://wiki.cobblemon.com/index.php/Spawn_Detail_Presets

5. Historical Change & Reimplementation Audit
A critical rule for this section: Cobblemon changelogs frequently say what changed but not why. When the official record gives a reason, that reason is preserved. When it does not, the 'why' column is explicitly marked as not stated. ER recommendations are separate from historical reasons.

6. Removed, Reworked or Superseded Concepts Worth Preserving

7. Reward Design Catalog for Ecological Resonance
The goal of this section is not to finalize rewards. It is a menu of reward primitives that can be attached to quests, restoration milestones, research discoveries, faction reputation, events, exploration, tournaments and emergent phenomena. The strongest ER reward economy should mix power, utility, identity, cosmetics, discovery and world change so that every reward does not become 'another item.'

7.1 Especially strong ER reward ideas
Restoration reward: the restored area itself becomes the reward — new Pokémon, flora, NPCs, shops, routes or structures appear.
Habitat unlock: completing a restoration chain unlocks a native Cobblemon Habitat structure or a new habitat population.
PC wallpaper: each major restored biome, faction, legendary domain or research milestone unlocks a themed wallpaper.
Research specimen: a guaranteed encounter with a species needed to continue a research question, rather than a generic loot chest.
Mark reward: a custom ER mark such as a restoration/provenance mark, provided it does not replace or corrupt Cobblemon's native mark system.
Event ticket: unlock a Pokémon rally, fishing tournament, Alpha migration, archaeology expedition, battle festival or ecological phenomenon.
Food recipe: a regional dish or restorative recipe tied to the place where it was discovered.
Resonance treatment: instead of giving a finished overpowered item, reward the ability/material needed to attune an existing item.
Display reward: plaque, fossil display, Pokémon portrait, PC wallpaper, trophy, pedestal, memorial or championship record.
Access reward: faction laboratory, Ranger outpost, research center, forge, habitat station, gym, battle tower or restoration workshop.
Knowledge reward: a new spawn clue, evolution clue, Move Dex entry, legendary-domain clue or ecological observation.
Pokémon reward with a story: a rescued, adopted, relocated or specially marked Pokémon rather than a random 'loot Pokémon'.
Cosmetic transformation: restore an existing object rather than hand out another object — e.g. ruined station becomes functional.
Community reward: a multiplayer restoration completion changes the shared world for everyone while personal rewards remain individual.
Negative-to-positive reversal: purifying a corrupted area can convert a dangerous encounter table into a healthy rare-spawn table.
7.2 Reward categories to avoid overusing
Flat currency as the default reward for every quest.
Permanent percentage stat boosts with no tradeoff.
Universal catch-rate increases that make specialized balls obsolete.
Random loot crates as the primary legendary/research reward.
Endless stacks of generic materials for story milestones.
Rewards that force every player into the same build.
Multiple new meters/currencies that exist only to justify rewards.
8. What Cobblemon Gives ER for Free vs. What ER Still Needs

9. Reimplementation Priorities After This Audit
Do not recreate a native Cobblemon feature merely because it appeared on an older ER brainstorm list. First ask whether 1.8.0 already supplies it.
Use native Type Gems, habitats, marks, PC wallpapers, riding, fishing, cooking and AI as building blocks.
Build ER primarily as a data/event/spawn layer around Cobblemon.
Use spawn rules and spawn conditions as the primary technical interface for World Affinity-driven population changes.
Use Habitat Blocks/structures for discrete restoration sites and major biodiversity milestones.
Use NPC party pools, compositions and dialogue for factions, researchers, Rangers and event hosts.
Use PC wallpapers, marks, plaques, display cases and world changes as non-power rewards.
Use Type Gems as the benchmark against which every new ER material must prove its distinct purpose.
Use native Alpha Pokémon as the natural 'exceptional population' state instead of inventing a second Alpha system.
Keep Fusion/Fractured/Shadow as custom ER systems because Cobblemon's current native features do not provide that complete synthesis/corruption architecture.
Keep breeding, where not fully implemented as a survival feature, out of assumptions until verified in the exact 1.8.0 build and desired sidemod stack.
Treat developer APIs as part of the pack's architecture, not merely technical trivia.
